gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns nondifferentiability of the objective and the resulting gradient definition at zero Fourier coefficients. It does not diagnose the distinct revised-exit-wave construction error in which a spatial component is substituted for a missing Fourier phase, nor does its repair specify completing the Fourier vector and applying one inverse transform.

ISSUE-004 diagnoses a coarse-grid MGPS coefficient becoming 0/0 or ill-conditioned when the averaged coarse probe vanishes. Gold I002 instead concerns the generic PIE/rPIE update for arbitrary u, where u+|Q|^2 can vanish and the quadratic minimization and quotient fail. These are different formulas, domains, and missing hypotheses.

ISSUE-001 notes objective nondifferentiability and an ill-defined or prior-iterate-dependent gradient at exact zeros, but it does not recognize the separate phase-selector defect: testing phase equality can trigger on nonzero positive-real coefficients, while testing phase at a zero is itself undefined, followed by an incorrect spatial overwrite. Its proposed differentiability qualification is not the specific phase-recursion repair.

Both identify that the theorem states an equivalence between objective-value equality and stationarity, while the proof supports only equality implying stationarity; the reverse implication is false. ISSUE-002 also supplies a counterexample and the exact one-way repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The theorem incorrectly asserts both directions of the equality/stationarity equivalence; only objective equality implying stationarity is established, while stationarity does not imply equality of successive objective values.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem claims an iff/equivalence, but the proof establishes only equality of successive objective values implying stationarity.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference from equality of a quadratic expression involving the restricted or bin-averaged gradient to vanishing of the full fine-grid gradient. The restriction has a nontrivial kernel, so equality yields only restricted stationarity.
